source.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Function Field Arithmetic — The Influence of John Tate’s Work

accepted.question_text: What are the complete algebraic relations among the multizeta values ζ(s1, …, sk) over A = Fq[t], where these multizeta values are defined by summing 1/(n1^s1 ··· nk^sk) over monic polynomials n1, …, nk in A with strictly decreasing degrees? In particular, which relations replace the classical sum-shuffle and integral-shuffle relations in positive characteristic, and how should the additional digit-phenomena constraints be formulated?

evidence.quote: The relations satisfied by them are under investigation. These relations are not quite the classical sum-shuffle and integral-shuffle relations and involve subtle ‘digit phenomena’.

accepted.question_text: What is the correct fundamental-group framework, over function fields, that explains the analogues of Ihara power series, Deligne-Soulé cocycles, higher circular units, and multizeta values in the same way that the Grothendieck-Ihara program and mixed Tate motives over Q explain these objects for the projective line minus three points?
accepted.context_brief: Fundamental-group background for function-field Ihara theory

evidence.quote: Ihara power series occurs in Grothendieck-Ihara program of the study of absolute Galois group over Q by realizing it in the automorphism group of the algebraic fundamental group of the projective line minus three points. ... We have these ingredients, as we have the mixed Tate-motives theory in function fields, but we have no good understanding of the fundamental group background yet!

accepted.question_text: For the Goss zeta function over A = Fq[t], whose interpolation includes both positive and negative integers, what functional equation should connect the special values at positive integers to the special values at negative integers, and how should the function-field gamma factors enter as the factor at infinity in such a functional equation?
accepted.context_brief: Functional equation for Goss zeta values

evidence.quote: David Goss (see [Gos96]) interpolated the zeta values at positive integers above to a much larger continuous space containing, in particular, the negative integers.

But still no functional equation connecting the two sets of values is understood in contrast to the Riemann zeta function functional equation whose nice analysis was done in Tate’s thesis. We do have good analogs [Tha04] of Gamma functions, but do not understand them as a factor at infinity for zeta as in Tate’s thesis.

accepted.question_text: What is the correct general description of the orders of vanishing of function-field zeta functions at negative integers, including an explanation of the systematic extra-vanishing phenomena that depend on the digit combinatorics of the integer s and on Weierstrass gaps?
accepted.context_brief: Orders of vanishing at negative integers

evidence.quote: Classically, a simple analysis of poles of gamma factors occurring in the functional equations of general zeta functions leads to determination of orders of vanishing of zeta functions at negative integers. In function fields, the story is not even conjecturally fully understood. There is some interesting systematic ‘extra vanishing’ phenomena of zeta at −s depending on digit combinatorics of s and Weierstrass gaps [Tha04, Sec. 5.4] and [Gos].

accepted.question_text: As E ranges over elliptic curves defined over Q, are the arithmetic ranks and analytic ranks of E(Q) bounded, or can they become arbitrarily large?

evidence.quote: It is not known whether the (arithmetic or analytic) ranks of E(Q) are bounded as E runs through elliptic curves E over Q, the usual bet seems to be that they are not.

accepted.question_text: For the ℘-adic interpolation of the arithmetic gamma function constructed by Goss, what is the general transcendence or algebraicity theory for its values, beyond the partial results currently known?
accepted.context_brief: General case of ℘-adic arithmetic gamma interpolation

evidence.quote: For the ℘-adic interpolation due to Goss of the gamma, Yao and myself only managed partial results [Tha04, Cha. 11], and the general case is still open.

accepted.question_text: What is the arithmetic nature of the values taken by the ℘-adic interpolations associated with the Carlitz-Goss arithmetic gamma function, what algebraic dependence relations hold among the special values of this arithmetic gamma function, and how do these questions extend both to arbitrary global function fields and to the other gamma function discussed in Sections 8.3 and 8.7 of Thakur’s book on function field arithmetic?
accepted.context_brief: Open questions on arithmetic gamma values

evidence.quote: There are still many open questions about the nature of values of ℘-adic interpolations, algebraic dependence relations for the Carlitz-Goss arithmetic gamma function mentioned above as well as their generalizations to arbitrary function fields, and for another gamma function developed in [Tha04, Sec.8.3, 8.7].

needs_review.question_text_raw: Open questions about distribution of Diophantine approximation exponents of algebraic elements and about their continued fraction expansions.

evidence.quote: For connections with deformation theory and many interesting recent results and open questions about distribution of Diophantine approximation exponents of algebraic elements and about their continued fraction expansions, we refer to [Tha04] and [Tha].
